articles.title: England can take vital lessons from worst defeats into Rugby World Cup, says Johnson
articles.summary: Former captain says losses can benefit team next year. Johnson refuses to comment on Henry Pollock hype. Martin Johnson believes England’s most painful defeats under Steve Borthwick can benefit them at the Rugby World Cup in Australia next year.
body: England endured some disastrous moments during the Six Nations this year, most notably the 42-21 defeat by Ireland at Twickenham, and finished the tournament with a solitary win against Wales. Summer Nations Championship fixtures began with an away defeat by the world champions, South Africa, before victories against Fiji and Argentina.

With a year until the tournament – England’s opener is scheduled for 2 October against Tonga in Brisbane – Johnson acknowledged the Six Nations was “up and down” under Borthwick but said vital lessons must be taken from the defeats.

“The bad experiences, the losing, it’s not wasted experience,” said Johnson, who captained England to the Rugby World Cup in 2003, and was head coach from 2008 to 2011. “You always want to win and they’re horrible at the time, but it shouldn’t be a wasted experience. All experience, good or bad, should go into your memory bank as a player.
points: Former captain says losses can benefit team next year.

articles.title: Tuchel praises Alexander-Arnold for ‘decisive’ display on England return
articles.summary: ‘We need to keep focused, and Trent was a big help in this’ Alexander-Arnold set up opener in 2-0 win over Czechia. Thomas Tuchel praised Trent ­Alexander-Arnold after the right-back impressed on his first England appearance since June 2025.
body: Alexander-Arnold, who has a point to prove after missing out on a World Cup spot, was one of the big positives as Tuchel’s side recovered from their defeat to Spain by recording a comfortable 2-0 win away to Czechia in the Nations League on Tuesday.

The Real Madrid defender shone in possession, particularly after the Czechs lost Pavel Sulc to a red card at 0-0, and helped England take the lead when he crossed for Anthony Gordon to score early in the second half.

“We never doubted that he can produce these kind of assists,” Tuchel said. “I think the second half the position, a bit of a deeper position, suited him more than the higher position in the first half. Overall, I think we had a good and professional performance. Of course the red card is such a heavy influence in the game.

“We need to keep focused, and Trent was a big help in this, because he’s very secure on the ball and can be decisive with his crosses. He did this solid defending and one decisive action that helped us score, so a good performance overall.”

articles.title: I'd stick my Man City medals in bin - Keane
articles.summary: Roy Keane says he would throw his "medals in the bin" if he were a Manchester City player after the club were found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.
body: Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane has said he would throw his "medals in the bin" if he were a Manchester City player after the club was found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.

On Tuesday, the Premier League confirmed the Etihad club had been found guilty of flouting its rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018 by creating "sham" contracts with commercial partners to secretly funnel more than £830m into their football operations.
City, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, won eight trophies, including three Premier League titles, during that period.
Keane said the achievements of City's players had become redundant because of the "cheating" that took place during that time.

articles.title: Nations League roundup: Lamine Yamal sinks Croatia in Spain’s World Cup homecoming
articles.summary: Teenager scores twice in 4-1 win to boost Ballon d’Or case. Slovenia beat North Macedonia; Faroe Islands hold Moldova. Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League in their first home game since lifting the World Cup.
body: Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring within two minutes against England in Saturday’s Wembley win and took just 75 seconds to do so against Slaven Bilic’s side in Andalusia. The teenager’s left-footed finish took his tally of international goals to nine in 36 appearances.
Just before the half-hour mark, the visitors equalised through Dion Beljo’s header as the 6ft 4in attacker headed home from an Ivan Perisic cross.

Two minutes later the hosts restored their lead as Marc Pubill fired home a header from a pinpoint Lamine Yamal cross before provider turned scorer again on 63 minutes, beating Barcelona teammate and Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic at his near post. With fewer than two minutes to play Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams notched up a fourth for Spain with a crisp dribble and finish.
Lamine Yamal’s contribution strengthened his case for the Ballon d’Or, with voting having closed on Monday and the winner announced on 26 October.

articles.title: Gordon and Kane fire England to Nations League victory against 10-man Czechia
articles.summary: Anybody can lose to Spain. But when England did so at Wembley on Saturday, it served to turn up the temperature for this trip to Czechia. England have form for finding it difficult at this compact stadium. Remember the European Championship qualifier here in 2019 when they lost 2-1?
body: It was not easy at first. Thomas Tuchel shuffled his pack, making the surprise decision to start Jude Bellingham among the substitutes. It was all a little angsty and Czechia, for whom this is the dawn of a new era under the Spaniard Santi Denia after their World Cup wipeout, dared to dream of another upset.

Then everything changed. It was a rash challenge in the 23rd minute by Pavel Sulc on Elliot Anderson, late and high, albeit nothing overtly nasty. The referee, Umut Meler, showed the Czechia midfielder a yellow card and on we went. Yet the VAR was not happy and when Meler was called to the pitchside monitor, everybody knew what was coming next.

It was a red card to disfigure the contest but Tuchel was not complaining. His players made the most of the decision to get their Nations League campaign up and running with the standout moment being provided by Tuchel’s headline selection.

articles.title: Hampden debut to forget but Pocognoli looks at bigger picture
articles.summary: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli hopes "we will remember this night differently later on" as his Hampden bow ends with a 3-0 defeat by Switzerland.
body: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli hopes to "remember this night differently later on" after his Hampden debut ended in a deflating Nations League defeat by Switzerland.
Off the back of a goalless draw in Ljubljana on Saturday in his first game as Scotland boss, Pocognoli's side slumped to a 3-0 loss in Glasgow's southside on Tuesday.
Scotland are now without a clean sheet in eight home matches and, perhaps more worryingly, have failed to score in six of their nine games this year.
Pocognoli promised a more attacking approach, built on a high press and high energy, but those ideals were undermined by Jack Hendry's 11th-minute red card.

articles.title: The intricate web Man City spun to con the Premier League
articles.summary: The 40-page document which confirmed Manchester City were found guilty of inflating sponsorship income makes fascinating reading. Here's what it sets out.
body: "To cheat, trick, deceive, delude with false pretences; to impose upon, take in, hoax."

And that word appears eight times in the independent commission's ruling published on Tuesday, which found Manchester City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of financial rules, and all but one in relation to a failure to co-operate with the investigation.
It catalogues how the club's owners, Abu Dhabi United Group, knew from the 2009-10 season that there would be major overspends if the club was to reach the level they wanted to get to.
So, the ruling says, City found a way to boost sponsorship income. Season, after season, after season.

articles.title: Nikola Topic, Thomas Sorber provide injury updates ahead of 2026-27 training camp
articles.summary: After the Oklahoma City Thunder went through an offseason of roster changes, they're expecting a recast around the supporting characters. For the first time in a couple of years, the role players will be new and different.
body: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams suffice as one of the top and most accomplished trios in the game. Those three should keep the Thunder in the contention picture for the foreseeable future. That said, the rest of the roster is filled with question marks.

Two of those remain with an injury tag. Sorta, at least. Nikola Topic and Thomas Sorber will be limited in training camp. Remains to be seen what that means for the 2026-27 regular season. The good news is, though, neither are limited because of a new injury. Instead, it's about ramping up after a long time of being out.

Topic was the No. 12 pick of the 2024 NBA draft. He's logged 10 career games. He missed the 2024-25 season with a torn ACL. He then missed most of the 2025-26 season with a testicular cancer diagnosis. Most of his 2026 offseason was spent in recovery. He had back surgery in June 2026.

Meanwhile, Sorber was the No. 15 pick of the 2025 NBA draft. He missed the final month of his collegiate season at Georgetown due to foot surgery. He missed the 2025-26 season with a torn ACL. He then had a second knee procedure done in July 2026. That knocked him out for most of the 2026 offseason.

For the first time in a couple of years, the role players will be new and different.

articles.summary: Luke Humphries was not punished for a raft of missed finishing doubles as he beat a below-par Dave Chisnall to reach the second round of the World Grand Prix in Leicester.
body: Humphries - who has made the last three finals in this event, winning in 2023 ahead of two runners-up finishes since - is the new favourite to triumph this year following defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night.

Cool Hand, sporting a scab on his forehead he put down to an allergic reaction, defeated Chisnall 2-0 while averaging only 80.41 and going at 26 per cent on his doubles as he secured a second-round meeting with Chris Dobey's conqueror Jermaine Wattimena.
Chisnall had a chance to break Humphries and push for a deciding set only to bust his score, before the world No 2 wrapped up victory on double four and then appeared to shush someone in the crowd.

Dobey was one of two seeds to tumble on Tuesday evening, alongside Josh Rock, who fell to Niels Zonneveld as the Dutch debutant peeled off three ton-plus finishes in the third set to book a last-16 date with Gary Anderson.

articles.summary: When the NFL released the schedule, we all keyed in on the first six weeks of the Denver Broncos season. body: Many of us fans we hoping that they'd come out of this stretch at or above.500 and so far it has been mission accomplished. It didn't look that way after the beat down in Kansas City, but the team bounced-back and are now ahead of the sticks in this stretch.

The toughest game left on this stretch of games is this week against the San Francisco 49ers. I am very doubtful they can get past them this week, but I see the next two games as quite doable. The Seattle Seahawks haven't been dominant to start the season and the Los Angeles Chargers are a dumpster fire presently. My target remains 4-2. If they get through these six games at 4-2, then they should be easily in the mix in the AFC come December.

articles.title: Gordon-inspired England seal much-needed win over Czech Republic
articles.summary: Pavel Sulc's first-half red card helped England recover from a nervy start to register an Anthony Gordon-inspired 2-0 Nations League win over the Czech Republic in Prague.
body: While the Three Lions toiled in the early stages and nearly fell behind twice to presentable chances wasted by Sulc, Barcelona winger Gordon, supported by former Newcastle team-mate Lewis Hall, was a threat throughout. He came close to teeing up an opener while the two sides were still 11 vs 11, but saw Morgan Rogers curl his low cross against the far post on the turn.

Even once Sulc had been dismissed following a VAR review for a studs-up challenge on the shin of Elliot Anderson, it took a reshuffle from Thomas Tuchel and the half-time arrival of Eberechi Eze for many of his team-mates to catch up following a particularly nervous and passive opening period from the Three Lions.

But once they did, it was Gordon who took full advantage less than two minutes after the restart to stoop and turn Trent Alexander-Arnold's typically inviting cross home, netting for the third competitive game in a row.

articles.title: Wigan dominate awards! O'Neill named Man of Steel; Foubister claims women's title
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors swept the major categories as Brad O'Neill was crowned 2026 Super League Man of Steel and Jenna Foubister was named the Woman of Steel.
body: Wigan's men's head coach Matt Peet and women's head coach Denis Betts, meanwhile completed a great night for the club with both picking up Coach of the Year awards.

Combative hooker O'Neill had already claimed the Rugby League Writers and Broadcasters Association (RLWBA) Player of the Year awards, having helped Wigan to the League Leaders' Shield, the Challenge Cup and came within 80 minutes of the Grand Final.

With his tough-tackling, pinpoint passing and impressive durability, the 24-year-old has developed into an integral part of Peet's side. He saw off Warriors team-mate Adam Keighran and Leeds Rhinos' Lachie Miller to take the crown.
Foubister also overcame a couple of Wigan team-mates in nominees Eva Hunter and Megan Williams to be named Woman of Steel.
